`gen_ai.inference.client` already defines `name.note` (including the additional guidance lines). Adding a `name.note` override in this refinement duplicates (and slightly diverges from) the base span-name guidance, which undermines the goal of removing duplicated text and makes future edits error-prone. Prefer inheriting the base span's `name` unless the provider truly needs a different naming rule.

This issue also appears on line 709 of the same file.

 span_refinements:
   - id: openai.inference.client
     ref: gen_ai.inference.client
+    name:
+      note: >
+        **Span name** SHOULD be `{gen_ai.operation.name} {gen_ai.request.model}`.

threads.body: Fine by me if this is the accepted cost of dropping the workaround, but flagging the trade explicitly: there's no caching left here at all. Weaver clones a remote vdir into a `TempDir` under `~/.weaver/vdir_cache` and deletes it when the `VirtualDirectory` is dropped (`create_tmp_repo` in `weaver_common/src/vdir.rs`), so nothing is reused between runs, local weaver or Docker -- the container mounts only `$(CURDIR):/workspace`. `make check-policies` now clones the policy pack from GitHub on every invocation and can't run offline, where the stamped `.build/weaver-policies` checkout it replaces was fetched once per `POLICY_REPO_REF`.
threads.hunk:
@@ -129,12 +113,12 @@ $(SC_UPSTREAM_STAMP): $(VERSION_PINS_FILE)
 
 filter-upstream: $(SC_UPSTREAM_STAMP)
 
-# Validate the model and run shared policies
-check-policies: $(LOCAL_POLICY_STAMP) $(SC_UPSTREAM_STAMP)
+# Validate the model and run shared policies from otel-weaver-packages.
+check-policies: $(SC_UPSTREAM_STAMP)
 	$(WEAVER) registry check \
 		-r ./model \
 		--v2 \
-		--policy $(LOCAL_POLICIES)/policies/check \
+		--policy '$(POLICY_REPO_URL)@$(POLICY_REPO_REF)[policies/check]' \

threads.body:
This same fix already landed on main in #405, as `attribute.provenance.path` -- that's what the conflict is. Suggest taking main's form so the only delta left here is your (clearer) comment above.

Related, and worth checking before merge: #405 also widened the in-sync check from `git diff --exit-code -- ./docs/registry` to `-- ./docs`, and this branch's base predates that commit. So the green `generated-docs` run here never verified `docs/gen-ai/*.md` -- exactly the files this PR regenerates. Worth re-running `make generate-all` after merging main.

```suggestion
[`{{ name(attribute) | trim }}`]({% if attribute.provenance.path %}{{ attribute_registry_base_url }}/{{ ns_id | kebab_case }}.md{% else %}{{ upstream_docs_base }}/docs/registry/attributes/{{ ns_id | kebab_case }}.md{% endif %})
```

Now that refinements inherit `name` from the base span, this override is the duplication the PR is removing. `azure.ai.inference.client` and `aws.bedrock.inference.client` have no `name` and fall through to the base note -- which is why aws-bedrock.md and azure-ai-inference.md gained the guidance in this PR.

Keeping the override leaves openai/anthropic with the one-line wording and bedrock/azure with the full three-sentence one, for the same span, in sibling docs. The first sentence is identical to the base anyway; the override only drops the "MAY specify different span name format" and "MUST follow the overall guidelines" sentences.

Deleting it means openai.md picks up the base text, so this needs a `make generate-all`.

```suggestion
```

i'll push back on this one. This would put free-form text for span.note under free-form text about span name resulting in something like 

> **Span name** SHOULD be `invoke_agent {gen_ai.agent.name}` if `gen_ai.agent.name` is readily available.
When `gen_ai.agent.name` is not available, it SHOULD be `invoke_agent`.
Semantic conventions for individual GenAI systems and frameworks MAY specify different span name format.
>
> Examples: LangChain agents, CrewAI agent

"Examples: LangChain agents, CrewAI agent" is a span note that has nothing to do with span name, but reads as a part of it.
